items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: that really came from conversations with all — I mean Miles Davis, Sonny Rollins, Art Blakey, anybody you talk to will tell you that.

ctx.x: That’s funny, I think of it the other way around. All the interviews that I’ve done have really affected my playing in that the takeaway from so many of the people I’ve talked to is the first thing that people tell you which is be yourself, you know, if you’re trying to

sound like somebody else you’re doomed to be second best, they’re already doing it. So at some point I really settled into owning my playing and not worrying about whether it was I don’t know, authentically part of the tradition or — I stopped comparing my performance and the time I put in and my practicing — I stopped comparing it with my hopes and dreams from being a 13-year-old kid or whatever, and just accepted it, and that really came from conversations with all — I mean Miles Davis, Sonny Rollins, Art…

Did you have a particular question, you sort of just answered it but it was specific to Miles, but I have a question that I usually ask about improvising, what are you thinking about when you’re improvising. And I almost always get the same basic answer. I’m not going to say what it is, I mean I could, but I wonder if you’ve had questions like that, that you usually find the same answer?
